headline._: CISA's listing runs through every page. A honeypot shows the flaws work; no organisation says it was breached.
headline.exec: Nothing new for you. Still no organisation says it was hit. The deadline to ask your team: 29 October.
headline.general: Nothing changes for you today. Websites that were patched stay safe; no company has said it was broken into.
headline.security: A researcher's honeypot (PHP 8.4.26, unpatched) was taken over: a decoy, not a victim. Unit 42's attack claim withdrawn. A fourth incident, Square Enix's, joins the open list; none is tied to php2shell.
headline.engineer: Nothing new to install. The honeypot ran an unpatched 8.4.26: confirm your build is the fixed one, after the restart.
headline.journalist: "Exploited" (CISA) is not "hacked". Two vendor claims of successful attacks are now withdrawn (Sophos, Unit 42); the honeypot is a lab. Four incidents stay open, none tied to php2shell.
headline.researcher: 645 sources by 19:13 UTC. Compromise ledger: the honeypot, Unit 42's retraction, Zscaler's decoy counts, CERT.LV's no-success line; four open candidates, none tied to php2shell.

items.text: The newsroom opens BREAKING-001: every page and record that CISA's listing touches is checked and dated.

A researcher's honeypot is taken over through the flaws: a decoy running an unpatched PHP 8.4.26, in a setup built to be easy; not an organisation, not a victim. The newsroom had it at 08:41 UTC, and later read it as 35 working shells in a favourable setup.
The readers' answers move to 00:45 UTC on 27 October, with CISA's listing: "Is it being exploited?" now answers yes, per CISA, from 26 October.
"Has anyone actually been hacked through php2shell?" gets a dated update: CISA's listing names no victim; still no organisation confirms a compromise.
Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 retracted on 25 October its claim that an attack on a European government agency came through PHP2Shell: it could not confirm the way in. The newsroom had it at 11:12 UTC.
items.src: SC Media (26 October), via the journalist

items.text: Attempts, not break-ins: Zscaler's decoys saw 1,156 attempts from 156 addresses in the first 48 hours; CERT.LV says no successful attack has been recorded in Latvia.
items.src: Fortune India (Zscaler, second-hand); Jauns.lv, LETA (CERT.LV); the journalist

items.text: Square Enix joins the open candidates: TechGaming.it, citing Kotaku, says it confirmed unauthorised access, without saying how. No source ties it to php2shell.
